component.name: Spola
component.summary: Keep your folders in sync with Koofr
Sincronizza le tue cartelle con Koofr

description.p: Spola keeps folders on your computer and folders on Koofr identical, in both directions, in the background. It is built on rclone's two-way sync and puts the safety of your files first.

Spola mantiene identiche, in entrambe le direzioni e in background, le cartelle del tuo computer e quelle su Koofr. Usa la sincronizzazione a due vie di rclone e mette al primo posto la sicurezza dei tuoi file.

ul.li: A preview of the first alignment before anything happens
Un'anteprima del primo allineamento prima che succeda qualsiasi cosa
Stops and asks before deleting many files at once
Si ferma e chiede prima di eliminare molti file insieme
Files changed on both sides: both versions are kept
File cambiati da entrambe le parti: restano entrambe le versioni
Replaced and deleted files are kept in a local backup for 30 days
I file sostituiti ed eliminati restano in un backup locale per 30 giorni
Add a folder by browsing your Koofr folders, with suggestions
Aggiungi una cartella sfogliando quelle su Koofr, con dei suggerimenti
Sync status and a Koofr menu in Files, Nemo, Caja and Dolphin; the Koofr menu in Thunar
Stato della sincronizzazione e menu Koofr in File, Nemo, Caja e Dolphin; il menu Koofr in Thunar
Status icon in the tray, notifications only when something needs you
Icona di stato nel tray, notifiche solo quando serve

description.p: Spola is not affiliated with Koofr.
Spola non è affiliata a Koofr.

In cima cosa sta succedendo, i file in sincronizzazione, poi le tue cartelle, raggruppate per dove si trovano

La pagina di una cartella: stato, le due posizioni, pausa, esclusioni

I conflitti: entrambe le versioni, una scelta per ciascuno
Resolving all conflicts with one rule
Tutti i conflitti risolti con una regola

Lo stato di ogni file in File

description.p: The sharing update for Linux and Windows: manage public links, passwords, expiration dates and invitations from Share in the file manager. Windows release checks use a portable temporary configuration file for rclone.

Share from the file manager opens a window showing who has access. Create, copy and revoke public links, manage their password and expiration, or invite people with view, edit or custom permissions. Inherited access stays visible, and opening the window or copying a link never publishes anything or changes permissions. Sharing settings are read back from Koofr after changes, including partial failures.

A deletion preview no longer needs a second confirmation when identical files have different dates. Windows Preferences opens at a manageable height and can be resized. Both Koofr trash dialogs show progress and let you stop and continue the search; failed pages resume without rereading earlier results, and slow responses use a shorter timeout. A whole deletion group can be restored only after the search is complete.

The window no longer stops for seconds with big folders (previews, restoring or opening a kept copy, Recently Deleted Files, a folder's page during a sync). On Windows, Add Folder offers the same place on Koofr as on this computer, and the window shows the home folder as "~" and groups the folders by where they are. On Linux, a file name that is not UTF-8 no longer takes the emblems of its whole folder. Koofr keeps previous versions of the files replaced there, as the window now says.

A Windows folder that went away and came back (a drive plugged in again) is watched again at once; "Later" in the update window no longer starts the installer when the download has just ended; a verification closed while it runs still says when everything matches; Preferences closed at once keeps the backup days just set; the menu of a conflict stays open while the folder syncs. Errors that passed in silence are said, the exclusions are saved whole or not at all, and rclone's fragments of a download cut short are removed after a day. The Koofr password never follows a redirect to another site, an update reads no more than the release says, and on Windows Spola runs only the rclone it ships.

From an independent review: identical files moved together keep their own dates (they were uploaded again with the other's), a confirmation no longer goes in circles when files are gone from both sides or changed the same way on both, the status shows the conflicts a run made at once, old backups are removed without freezing the window, and a safety stop says its reason in plain words; a previous version is restored once the sync in progress has finished. Windows updates install only the installer of the announced version, kept open until Setup has read it, and "Open a Copy" shows a program or a shortcut in its folder instead of running it.

Windows: Spola no longer stays "offline" with the network working (it asks Windows whether there is a network); the title bar's icon is sharp, drawn for its size; the status icons in the window match the notification area's; the text is a size larger.

Windows: much less memory (one change monitor for each synced folder, instead of one of half a megabyte for every folder inside it), and changes deep in a folder now honour the exclusions. A sleep that comes regardless of Spola (the lid closed, the battery low) stops the sync gracefully, and it goes again on waking. "Previous Versions…" and "Recently Deleted Files…" in File Explorer's menu. An update runs only an installer signed with Spola's own key.

Recently deleted files no longer wait for the whole of Koofr's trash: the files of the folder show as the trash is read, the newest deletions first, a page that times out is asked again instead of failing the whole reading, and the trash once read serves every window for a few minutes.

Previous versions, from the copies Spola keeps of what a sync replaces or deletes here: "Previous Versions…" on a file and "Recently Deleted Files…" on a folder in the file manager, and a Kept Copies section on each folder's page. A copy opens read-only, comes back as a copy next to the file or replaces it (the current file kept first, so it can be undone); recently deleted files also lists Koofr's trash. The next sync uploads what you restore. The copy not kept of a resolved conflict is kept there too. A kept copy is deleted only when it expires: the buttons that deleted backups by hand are gone.
New icons, in the common style of my logos.

A folder whose two sides already match no longer waits for a confirmation of its first alignment: the preview Spola prepares on its own finds nothing to copy, and the alignment goes on by itself. With anything to copy, the preview still asks.

For the desktop's own widgets: Spola keeps a small status file (status.json in its state folder) current with what it is doing, every folder's state and progress, for a shell widget such as the Noctalia plugin to show; and the icon in the notification area can be switched off in the preferences when such a widget takes its place.

The window no longer freezes while Spola reads the record of a large folder at start and after each of its syncs (close to a second for 40,000 files, now off the main loop), and a damaged record no longer stops Spola from starting: the folder asks for a repair instead. Renames by case alone inside nested folders were verified on Koofr itself.

Verify both sides: a folder's page compares every file here and on Koofr by size and checksum, changing nothing, and shows what is only here, only on Koofr, different or could not be compared, each as a tree; every confirmed alignment is followed by a verification of its own, with a word only if the sides differ. On the command line: spola verify.

Local backups, seen and used: the folder's page lists the backups of past syncs with their size, opens each as a tree, puts a file back in its place (the one there now kept first), deletes a backup or all of them. After every successful sync Spola keeps a copy of the synced state it reached: a repair can go back to that state and sync normally from there, with every safety check, instead of a new alignment. A damaged record of the last synced state now asks for a repair instead of retrying for ever.

Settings that survive accidents: every save keeps the previous file next to it, a damaged settings file is set aside and the previous save used (Spola says so at start), a file written by a newer Spola is read for what this version knows and written back whole, and a save that fails is said instead of swallowed.

Troubleshooting: the About window has a Troubleshooting page with versions, paths, every folder's state and last outcome, and the room the logs, listings and backups take, with a Save button; a folder's page opens the log of its last sync. Logs leave out the statistics lines past 50 MB and older logs are compressed, the newest kept readable.

A nearly full disk stops a sync before it starts, with a clear message: the disk of the folder must hold what a preview says would come down, with a margin; the disk holding Spola's own files must not be nearly full either.

Two more safety thresholds, from the audit. Deletions: the share of a folder a sync may delete unasked (10 percent by default) now also has a cap of about 500 files, so a folder of 40,000 files no longer allows 4,000 deletions without a word; a confirmed sync still deletes what its preview showed. Overwrites: a sync that would upload many files changed on this computer at once (a snapshot put back, a program rewriting a whole library, a restore from a backup) stops before it starts, says "N of T files changed on this computer at once" and waits for a look at the preview; the threshold is the folder's percentage, between 50 and 500 files. A confirmed sync may upload what its preview showed and little more: if more files change meanwhile, it asks again. The command line refuses such a sync the same way and says how to confirm it.

Reliability, from the audit: a sync asked for while one ran (a change on Koofr, a retry) no longer waits for the hourly check; a sync interrupted by a crash says so ("a previous sync was interrupted: trying again in 3 min") instead of an rclone message in red; a run that could not start stays an error until one does, and is tried again; pausing a folder cancels a sync still being prepared; stopping a confirmed sync while it is prepared leaves the folder waiting for its confirmation, not "up to date"; exclusions changed during a sync lead to a repair in Spola's words; a lost Koofr activity feed falls back to the periodic check whatever failed.

Previews: a file name with a quote or a backslash shows as its name, not as a quoted full path; a preview rclone counted but whose lines could not be read is refused rather than shown as "nothing to do"; a preview prepared ahead is prepared once, not again at every change of conditions. A restore from Koofr's trash puts back the dates only of files still the same here, by date and by Koofr's checksum. The folder monitor leaves the folder's own exclusions alone, and a folder too large to watch entirely says so. Lowering the backup retention asks first, saying how many backups and how much would go. Long syncs keep one line of statistics at a time instead of one a second.

A confirmation is worth what its preview showed, no more: a confirmed sync may delete the share of files the preview listed, with a small margin, instead of going past every limit; if more would go, it stops and asks again. A preview overtaken by a change (here, or on Koofr) can no longer be confirmed: the dialog says so and prepares it again.

The computer stays awake while a sync runs, on every Linux desktop (through logind, lid closed or not; a switch in Preferences turns it off), and a sleep that comes anyway stops the sync gracefully and starts it again after the wake. An unexpected failure while a run is prepared, followed or read no longer leaves a folder stuck in "Preparing…" or Spola unable to quit: it is reported as an error of that folder. Quitting waits for a preview being prepared too, and ends a stuck rclone after two minutes.
Nothing is published to the Flatpak repository, nor packaged for Windows, without the tests; the dialog tests now run in the build too.

A folder deleted or emptied on Koofr (from another computer, from the web), or emptied here, no longer shows as "needs a repair", which could not help: Spola says what happened ("is no longer on Koofr", "is empty on Koofr", "is empty on this computer") and offers what does: restore it from Koofr's trash, upload this computer's files again (after a preview), copy Koofr's files here again, or stop syncing it. The files on the other side are never touched meanwhile.
Fixed: a banner title with an apostrophe or an ampersand showed its markup ("c'è").

A preview also says how much of each folder a change touches: "the whole folder", or "31% of the folder", under every folder of the tree and for the whole synced folder on each kind of change. A folder deleted on another computer shows at once as gone entirely, next to one where only a few old files go.

A large preview is easy to read: each kind of change (copied to Koofr, deleted here...) opens on a page of its own as a tree of folders, each with how many files it holds and how big they are, open or closed at will. A deletion of twenty thousand files shows at once the two projects it touches, and no file is left out of the list any more.
Windows: on a monitor whose scale differs from the main one (a 250% monitor next to a 200% one), Windows scales the whole window, at the size of the other apps.

Files still being written (a transcription, a download, a file being exported) wait before they are synced: a new one is synced once it has settled, and for one already synced the sync waits for it, at most five minutes, saying which file it waits for. Synced half written, such a file looked changed on both sides at the next sync, and Spola could stop for a repair. Sync Now never waits.
Windows: on a monitor whose scale is not a whole number (125%, 150%, 250%), the text is as large as in the other apps.

The tray icon is always in the panel's own colour, like the panel's other icons: no more blue, orange or red. Its shape says what is going on: arrows while syncing, a mark when something needs you, a cross on errors. The window and the notifications keep the coloured status.

Windows: the window keeps the system title bar, so it snaps to the screen edges and to Win+arrows like any other. File Explorer shows a folder's status as soon as it is added, as other sync clients do: what is not yet in sync waits, each file turns green as soon as it is copied, never a green tick on a file changed since (while Spola was closed or paused), and what Spola leaves out shows no status. The status is on by default and can be turned off in Preferences; turned off, the files stay ordinary files. Folder names with emoji, read-only files and files open in Office get their status too.

Fixed: Stop, then Pause, Pause All or Quit ended rclone at once, and the next sync needed a repair; two folders empty at their first alignment could settle a file new on both sides by date, without a preview (now a repair, with its preview); a folder removed while its sync was being prepared left its state behind. Removing a folder removes its state, never its backups, and backups of removed folders expire as the others do.
Windows updates: the installer is downloaded only from Spola's releases, with its checksum checked; Setup closes only Spola's own programs.

Fixed: when many files changed only in their dates (put back from a backup, restored from Koofr's trash), a sync stopped half way could leave some of them missing on Koofr for a while. Koofr cannot change a file's date, and the copy on Koofr was deleted well before its new upload; now it is replaced only when its upload starts. Nothing was ever deleted on this computer, but another computer syncing the same folder could have deleted its copies.

Spola for Windows, a first version: an installer and a portable zip with this release, the status in the notification area and in File Explorer, Koofr's links from File Explorer, updates from the releases. Folders can now be taken over from Koofr Desktop in the window, on Linux and on Windows.

Restore from Koofr's trash, on a folder's page: what was deleted on Koofr in that folder, grouped by when, and the deletion you choose comes back, never the whole trash. Spola makes again the folders left empty, which the trash does not keep, and, since Koofr gives restored files today's date, uploads again the files identical to this computer's to put their dates back.

Fixed: a folder or a file renamed here by case alone ("Screencasts" to "screencasts") was not renamed on Koofr, which does not tell the two names apart. The preview counted its files as deleted on Koofr and uploaded again, and after the sync the files moved into it came back here in a second folder with the old name, and the folder stopped for a repair. Nothing was lost, but now Spola renames it on Koofr first, on the server, and the preview shows it as one move.

A confirmation no longer looks lost: a folder you confirm while another one syncs says at once "Confirmed, starts after the sync in progress", and the confirmed runs go in the order you gave them, before every automatic one. A preview left running in the background shows in the banner while it is prepared, then says it is ready, with the button to look at it.
When little space is left on Koofr, under 10%, the banner says how much remains.

A sync no longer looks stuck once its copies are done: when it goes on deleting files on Koofr, one at a time, the status says "Deleting: 2,000 of 8,148" and the bar moves again, then "Removing empty folders" while the folders left empty go. In the list of files, deleted folders are marked done as they go.

Fixed: after a big reorganisation, the preview counted thousands of conflicts that do not exist. rclone warns about every file new or changed on both sides, then finds most of them identical, or sees a folder made on both sides; only a file whose two copies it renames is a conflict, and only those are counted now, in the preview, in the files list and in the notifications.
Fixed: some Koofr paths kept a prefix like "koofr{kFw_7}:", so the moves of a reorganisation were also counted as uploads and deletions, and the lists showed full remote paths.

Fixed: a click on "Open Spola" in the tray menu could quit Spola. The menu's items were numbered by their place, and the place changes while a sync runs (a file done, the progress line gone): a tray that still showed the menu of a moment before sent the number that had become "Quit". Every item that does something now keeps its number wherever it moves, and a number is never given to another item.

Previews no longer hold anything up: they run next to the syncs of the other folders, the window stays usable, and you can close one and open it again at once, or cancel it for good. While it runs you see how far it is; when it is done it says how much goes each way and warns when Koofr has no room for it. A folder waiting for you has its preview prepared ahead (not on a metered connection), so Review opens it at once, and its row already says what it will do.

What waits for you is now in a banner under the header bar, and the status at the top keeps saying what Spola is doing: a folder waiting for its alignment no longer hides the others syncing. Large previews no longer freeze the window for a moment while rclone reports thousands of files.

A move stays a move: a file renamed or moved to another folder on one side is moved the same way on the other, on Koofr's server, instead of being deleted and copied again. A big reorganisation still stops for a confirmation, and its preview lists the moves as moves, not as deletions. Fixed along the way: after a file was renamed on Koofr, the next sync uploaded it again, because Koofr keeps modification times to the millisecond.

Many conflicts at once: Resolve All keeps the newer version, this computer's, Koofr's or both, after showing what happens to each file and leaving to you what the rule cannot decide. A rule can also resolve new conflicts on its own after each sync, for all folders in Preferences or for one folder on its page; the default is still to ask. The version not kept goes to the wastebasket here and to Koofr's trash.

Spola suggests names Koofr accepts for the files it refuses (the emoji taken out, "Contract (2).odt" for a name that differs only in case) and renames them once you confirm, from the list of files not synced or from the preview of a first alignment. A click on a file in a preview shows it in the file manager, or its folder on Koofr when it is only there.

Spola no longer syncs while Koofr Desktop runs on the same computer or is set to start at login: on one laptop the two engines on the same folders deleted a file on Koofr. Koofr Desktop on your other computers is fine.

Under the status at the top of the window, the files being synced, each with what is happening to it (download, upload, deletion on either side, conflict) and its progress. The tray icon shows the progress when you hover it and at the top of its menu. A sync started on its own stops when the network becomes metered, if Spola pauses there, and starts again when it no longer is. Align and Review no longer leave the window frozen for a few seconds on large folders, and the Flatpak follows the GTK 4 colours set by the desktop (Noctalia, for one).

Spola now works with the other common file managers: emblems and the Koofr menu in Nemo and Caja too, the Koofr menu in Dolphin and Thunar, and the overlay icons in Dolphin with a small plugin you build on your system. In Dolphin and Thunar the share link is shown by Spola with a Copy button. The emblems carry their colours for the file managers that do not recolour them, and the "left out" one no longer has a gap where the bar meets the ring.
Fixed: a change in a folder while its preview was running could queue a normal sync behind it, on a folder that was waiting for a repair.

A new window, after the GNOME guidelines: the folders grouped by where they are, the overall status at the top, a page for each folder. Adding a folder suggests the matching folder on Koofr and lets you browse your Koofr folders or create one. The tray icon stays quiet when everything is up to date, turns blue while syncing, orange or red when something needs you, and its menu lists the files being transferred and the last ones synced. Fixed: Files showed no emblems after Spola restarted, and the Flatpak installed the Files extension where Files does not look.

The site and the repository page in English, sharper screenshots including Files, and a few fixes: a hidden marker file now tells a synced folder from an empty one in its place (ext4 reuses inode numbers), and the progress line says "1 file" instead of "1 files".
First development version: one or more folder pairs, two-way sync with previews and safety stops, tray icon.
